title: "Loosen my tongue"
hookLine: Musa asks for an open chest, an easy task, a loosened tongue, and his brother Harun as help

cards: A phone call. A presentation. Telling your parents something.
Walking into a room where someone is angry with you. The chest goes tight, the mouth goes dry, the practiced words disappear. Now Musa gets his assignment: go to Pharaoh; he has transgressed.
The man whose house you grew up in. The man whose people you ran from, with a death on your hands. Musa doesn't say no.
He doesn't pretend he's fine either. He asks for help, very specifically, in four parts.

teach.b: Surah Ta-Ha. Rabbi ishrah li sadri. My Lord, expand my chest for me.
Then: make my task easy for me.

teach.h: UNTIE THE KNOT FROM MY TONGUE.
teach.b: Then: untie the knot from my tongue, so they understand what I say.
Then: give me a helper from my family, Harun, my brother. Strengthen me through him, and let him share my task. Look at the order.
He starts inside, with the chest, where fear sits and squeezes: give me room to breathe. Then the task, then the words, then a person. He doesn't ask for the task to go away.

He asks to be made big enough for it. That first line has a life of its own: Muslims say it before exams, job interviews, a hard conversation, a speech. The knot on his tongue: the Qur'an doesn't say what it was.
There's a well-known story that as a baby in Pharaoh's palace Musa put a burning coal in his mouth, and it left him slow of speech.
That story comes from the commentaries, not the Qur'an, so take it as a story people tell.
And the helper. The word is wazir: a helper, one who shares the load. Musa asks for his brother, so he doesn't have to walk into that palace alone.
A few verses later comes the answer: you have been granted your request, O Musa.

how: Muslims recite Musa's prayer from Surah Ta-Ha, rabbi ishrah li sadri, wa yassir li amri, before exams, speeches, interviews and difficult conversations.

o: a helper who shares the load
a rival who wants your place
a judge who settles a quarrel

games.q: what's inside the prayer — tap the pairs.
p: a helper who shares the load

s: the Qur'an says Musa burned his tongue on a coal as a baby
that's a story from the commentaries. the Qur'an says only that there was a knot on his tongue.
Musa asked for the task to be taken away
he asked for an open chest, an easy task, clear words and a helper, not to be excused.
Musa was told his request was granted
a few verses later: you have been granted your request, O Musa.

games.q: you're Musa. you've been told: go to Pharaoh. your chest is tight and your words don't come easily. what do you ask for first?
o: a bigger miracle to show Pharaoh.
games.why: he starts inside: expand my chest. then an easy task, a loosened tongue, and his brother Harun as helper. and he's told: your request is granted.

practice: Name the thing you dread, put a hand flat on your chest, and notice how tight it is; with each breath in, let your ribs widen a little, as if there were more room in there than you thought.

Then ask for one piece at a time: room inside, an easier task, the right words, and one person you could actually ask to come with you, or text first. If you pray, you can use Musa's words: rabbi ishrah li sadri.

wordCard.voice: Wazir, helper: the word Musa used asking for his brother Harun, so he wouldn't face Pharaoh alone.

orig.note: Arabic, from Qur'an 20:25: "my Lord, expand my chest for me."

carryVoice: Your line: expand my chest. He asked for room, not rescue. Fifty days, look at you.
